name: Structured Output Validator
blurb: a model's JSON answer checked against a schema, broken JSON repaired, and every error shown where it is
intro: Repairs the usual ways a model breaks JSON (fences and prose, comments, single quotes, bare keys, trailing or missing commas, Python literals, NaN, a cut-off tail) as steps you can switch off, parses the result strictly (RFC 8259) with every value's place kept, and checks it against a JSON Schema draft 2020-12 subset. Each repair and each schema error is marked where it is in the text, and a retry prompt tells the model exactly what to fix.

usage: Give `output` (the model's raw reply) and `schema` (a JSON Schema; draft 2020-12 keywords incl. type, properties, required, items/prefixItems, enum, const, min/max, minLength/maxLength, pattern, additionalProperties, oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not, if/then/else, local $ref). Repair steps are bools, all on by default. It returns a verdict, the repairs made (step, line, was, now), schema errors with JSON Pointers, line numbers and suggested fixes, and texts 'Repaired JSON', 'Errors' (JSON list) and 'Retry prompt' to send back to the model. Use it on any model output that must be machine-read, before trusting it.
sources: RFC 8259 The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format
JSON Schema Core and Validation, draft 2020-12 (json-schema.org/draft/2020-12): applicators §10, validation keywords §6, format as annotation §7.2.1
ECMA-262 regular expressions (pattern, with the u flag)
